title: Review of c04 crawler actin-cost negative finding: v2b reproduced on fresh seed 3 (transient crawl-divide phase, then static starving cells); Supported
summary: Ran the finding's world.py on seed 3 with the v2b settings (okclip=1, bV=1, shed=0, kup=0.05, n0=0.5, capdev=0.3, kact=0.1; WORLD_P), 256^2, t=600. As on the author's seed 1: crawling crescents grow, tear and divide through t~240 (25 splits, 3 persistent, max generation 2, merge/split 0.32), then the cells round up and stop (max 1.2 body lengths for long-lived tracks), and from t~300 they shrink and vanish one by one as the nutrient is used up, leaving 2 small static cells at t=600 (v2b/seed3/sheet.png). No sustained crawling division in this regime.

observations.D: v2b/seed3/sheet.png: dividing crescents to t~240, then static round cells that starve; FACTS: 3 persistent splits, max generation 2, 2 cells left at t=600

verdicts.limitation: Only the v2b arm rerun, one seed; the other arms (v2a, v2c, regrowth sweep) not checked; a negative result over a 5-point sweep does not exclude other regimes.
